title.en: Doppler effect: a moving listener, the general formula and uses

hook.en: Drive towards a factory siren and its note rises; drive away and it falls. This time the source is still. You are running into the waves.

objectives.en: Find f′ for a moving listener
Combine both motions in one formula

narration.en: Drive towards a factory siren and its note rises; drive away and it falls. This time the source is still. You are running into the waves.

title.en: A moving listener meets more crests

body.en: When the source is still, the wavelength is unchanged, $\lambda = v/f$. A listener moving towards it at $v_o$ meets crests at the relative speed $v + v_o$, so $f' = f\,\dfrac{v + v_o}{v}$. Moving away: $f' = f\,\dfrac{v - v_o}{v}$. With both moving along the line joining them: $f' = f\,\dfrac{v \pm v_o}{v \mp v_s}$ (upper signs for approach). If the medium (wind) moves at $w$ from source to listener, replace $v$ by $v + w$.

points.en: Listener moving: same λ, more crests per second
Only velocity components along the line joining them count

say.en: Start from the source at rest and the listener at rest: f prime equals f.
Top: the listener. Towards the source adds v o. Bottom: the source. Towards the listener subtracts v s.
Check: if v s equals v o and both move the same way, the factors cancel and f prime is f.

draw.tex: v_o = v_s:\; f' = f\frac{v - u}{v - u} = f

body.en: A police radar sends waves at a car and measures the shift of the echo; the car acts first as a moving listener and then as a moving source, so the shift is about twice that for one motion. Doppler ultrasound measures the speed of blood in the heart. Bats judge their prey from the shift of their echoes. Light from galaxies moving away is shifted to longer wavelengths (red shift).

steps.en: The listener moves towards a still source: f' = f (v + v_o)/v.

problem.en: A car sounding a 400 Hz horn moves at 20 m/s towards a wall. What is the frequency of the echo heard by the driver? (v = 340 m/s)

steps.en: The wall re-emits 425 Hz; the driver moves towards it: f₂ = 425 × (340 + 20)/340 = 450 Hz.
In one step: f₂ = f (v + u)/(v − u) = 400 × 360/320.

body.en: For an echo from a fixed wall when you move at u: f_echo = f (v + u)/(v − u). For small u, the shift is about 2u/v of f.

points.en: Listener moving: λ is unchanged; f′ = f (v ± v_o)/v.
General: f′ = f (v ± v_o)/(v ∓ v_s), upper signs for approach; only components along the line count.
Uses: radar speed guns, Doppler ultrasound, bats, red shift.
